title: Let GUI-started update prompts be answered with the mouse
head: 313900ae7f95
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: New helper loses its executable bit, so checkout updates cannot reach either confirmation
leads.consequence: The new test exits 126 at its first invocation. In a dev-linked checkout, `omarchy confirm` is unregistered (127), the initial update prompt calls a non-executable command and reports 'Update cancelled' before installing anything, while an update that bypasses the initial prompt gets permission denied at the reboot prompt. Packaged installation is different: omarchy-pkgs PKGBUILD:115-125 installs each bin with mode 755, so do not claim a packaged user gets this same permission error.

leads.summary: New fzf availability probe violates the bin-wide lint rule
leads.consequence: Every `test/shell` and `test/all` run fails at `bin-style-test.sh` because it finds `command -v` in the new helper, even though the new file is non-executable. Existing `omarchy-cmd-present fzf` is the repository's command probe (`bin/omarchy-cmd-present:5-7`). The packaging mode conversion does not fix this.
leads.triage: new; verified by coordinator source read (bin-style-test.sh:7-10, bin/omarchy-confirm:105) and Opus follow-up runs p5/p6

leads.summary: Rebase against current quattro: the shared reboot helper now guards unattended updates
leads.consequence: Current base tip 944fa24 contains a new `--services-only`/`--reboot-only` phased restart and, importantly, a `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1` early branch that reports rather than asking to reboot. The pinned PR replaces the old one-line `gum confirm`, so its patch does not apply to that new function; merging requires resolving the conflict while retaining BOTH the unattended guard and the new mouse helper in only the interactive branch. Taking this PR's function wholesale would prompt and potentially reboot during `omarchy update -y`, including a pseudo-TTY from script(1); dropping the PR branch would lose mouse input at reboot.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus N3 (quattro conflict); GitHub mergeable_state dirty

leads.summary: Gum's additional toggle keys are not migrated, and Shift+Tab does not move at all
leads.consequence: Gum confirm accepts h, l, Ctrl+N, Ctrl+P and Shift+Tab as toggles in addition to Left/Right/Tab. This PR explicitly maps only left/right/tab. fzf 0.74.3's default Shift+Tab is toggle-up, a no-op when --multi is not set; h/l are not bound in inputless mode. A user who used Shift+Tab, h or l on default Yes then presses Enter now confirms Yes instead of switching to No, including on the update prompt. Ctrl+N/P happen to move rows by default but should be covered so their behaviour is not assumed to match gum in other states; add explicit binds and a real-fzf check of every key.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus M1 (h/l/Shift-Tab); Ctrl-N/P already work per Opus

leads.summary: The public label arguments can make No indistinguishable from Yes
leads.consequence: Passing the same string to --affirmative and --negative creates two identical fzf rows; choosing the No row produces the affirmative text, returns 0, and any caller using `if omarchy-confirm` proceeds with the destructive operation. The fallback gum branch tests the selected boolean and would return 1 for No. Reject identical labels or preserve an independent answer ID instead of deciding by output string. The PR's fixed update prompts use default distinct labels, so this affects the advertised reusable `omarchy confirm` command after its mode is fixed.
leads.triage: source-confirmed ([[ $choice == $affirmative ]]); contrived identical-label edge case with no caller; dropped

limits: No real-fzf keyboard run: executable-bit failure stops the pinned test before its optional PTY case and sandbox PATH does not contain fzf. fzf 0.74.3 and gum v0.17 source provide keymap evidence.

Open PR searches for short/shared topic terms return many unrelated matches; focused overlap checked for #8992, #8724, #10865, #10232, #10524, #9511, #13444 and #12837; do not treat unexamined search hits as negative evidence.

flags.claim: The same commit introduced two problems that make test/shell fail and break the helper in a checkout
flags.why: Only the mode change breaks the helper in a checkout. The bin-style failure only fails test/shell; the helper runs fine once +x is restored.
flags.fix: 'two problems that make test/shell fail, one of which also breaks the helper in a checkout'

flags.claim: The new real-fzf test block catches the earlier test gaps
flags.why: The earlier optional test note had three parts. HOME isolation is still not addressed: run_confirm (confirm-test.sh:53-57) sets no HOME, and omarchy-restart-gum reads $HOME/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme/gum_env.lua.
flags.fix: Say it catches the stub-argument and start:pos gaps, and that HOME is still the runner's (or drop 'the earlier test gaps').

flags.claim: Dev-linked checkouts cannot confirm an update
flags.why: This holds only while no executable omarchy-confirm exists later in PATH. Once a package ships /usr/bin/omarchy-confirm, bash skips the non-executable file and runs the packaged copy instead, so the update is confirmable but the checkout's helper is silently ignored.
flags.fix: 'Dev-linked checkouts cannot confirm an update until a packaged omarchy-confirm exists, and then run that copy instead of the checkout's'

flags.claim: Suggested change: use the repository's helper, if ! omarchy-cmd-present fzf; then
flags.why: Incomplete suggestion. That change alone passes bin-style-test, but the PR's fallback case (PATH=$nofzf_bin with only gum and awk) then falls back because omarchy-cmd-present is missing ('command not found'), not because fzf is missing: with an fzf stub added to that dir it still ran gum. The test also comes to depend on an installed omarchy-cmd-present. With no omarchy-* on PATH the full test fails at 'confirm passes bind flags to fzf', and the real-fzf block passes all 5 cases while driving gum.
flags.fix: Add to the suggestion: link $ROOT/bin/omarchy-cmd-present into the no-fzf dir and put $ROOT/bin on the test's PATH (run_confirm and the python block).

flags.claim: fzf reads keys already pending at startup and handles them before both rows have loaded. pos(2) then lands on the only row present (Yes), and accept with no row exits 1.
flags.why: This does not always happen: n/q were right in 96-97 of 100 runs. The list state (one row present, or none and then loaded before the close request) is inferred from fzf source (vset clamps to current length, terminal.go:8752-8754; output at close prints the current row, 2241-2272; reqClose 6708-6714), not observed.
flags.fix: 'can handle them before both rows have loaded; pos(2) can then land on Yes, and accept with no row exits 1'

flags.claim: In a few percent of those cases the update or reboot goes ahead.
flags.why: Minor. 4/100 (n) and 3/100 (q) were measured only with the key already buffered before the helper started. The rate for a key pressed 'as the prompt appears' on a real terminal was not measured, which the scope line admits. Also, the pre-prompt output in omarchy-update-confirm is the 'Ready to update?' box, not an 'update summary'.
flags.fix: Tie the rate to the measured condition, for example 'with the key already typed, n or q answered Yes in 3-4 of 100 runs'.

flags.claim: taking this PR's version of the function as is would drop the unattended guard and prompt during omarchy update -y
flags.why: Minor lost qualifier. confirm_reboot is only called when a reboot is due (kernel updated, reboot-required flag, Hyprland replaced). This comes from quattro source; the PR-side resolution was not run.
flags.fix: '...and prompt during omarchy update -y when a reboot is due'

flags.claim: h:up,l:down,btab:up would match gum; l then Enter answers Yes where gum answers No
flags.why: The bind was not executed. Key names are valid per fzf options.go (single runes, 'btab'/'shift-tab' at 1116-1118). 'gum answers No' for l comes from gum 2.0.2 confirm.go:39-50 (Toggle includes l), not a gum run. Head behaviour (l, Enter -> 0) was run.

flags.claim: A deadline loop with os.WNOHANG that kills the child on expiry would make it fail cleanly
flags.why: Design suggestion, not implemented or run. The hang itself is verified.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on 313900ae. The four behaviour issues from the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12359#issuecomment-5832793408) are fixed, as described in the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12359#issuecomment-5842692115). The same commit introduced a file-mode change that breaks the helper in a checkout, a lint failure in `test/shell`, and a narrower keyboard race. The branch also now conflicts with `quattro`.

**Verified** with real fzf 0.74.3 in a pseudo-terminal, on an executable copy of the helper (see the first finding below):

| Earlier finding | Status at 313900ae |
|---|---|
| `n` then Enter answered Yes | Resolved: `y`/`Y` return 0; `n`/`N`/`q` return 1; Right, Left or Tab then Enter returns 1; Esc and Ctrl-C return 130 |
| fzf not a package dependency, all failures mapped to 130 | Resolved through the fallback: with fzf missing, `gum confirm` answers with the same labels and default; an invalid fzf option exits 2 with `fzf failed (exit 2)` |
| `--default=false` usually started on Yes | Resolved: Enter answered No in 60 of 60 runs (previous helper: Yes in 25 of 30 and 23 of 30) |
| `FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS` changed the answer | Resolved: `--tac`, `--print-query`, an options file and `--no-mouse` no longer change the answer or mouse reporting |

The new real-fzf test block catches most of the earlier test gaps: it fails on `--info=bogus`, on a removed `unset`, and on a `start:pos` mutant in 9 of 10 runs. The stub runs still read the runner's own `$HOME` theme file.

### `bin/omarchy-confirm` lost its executable bit

313900ae changes the file mode from 100755 to 100644. In a checkout:

```text
test/shell.d/confirm-test.sh   line 54: bin/omarchy-confirm: Permission denied   (exit 126)
omarchy confirm --help         Unknown Omarchy command   (exit 127; bin/omarchy registers only executable files)
omarchy-update-confirm         Permission denied, then "Update cancelled" without waiting for input
omarchy-update-restart         Permission denied, reboot offer skipped
```

The last two rows are with the checkout's `bin/` first on `PATH`, as `omarchy dev link` sets it. With `chmod 755`, the PR's test passes in full.

**Impact:** packaged installs are not affected, because the PKGBUILD installs every `bin/*` with `install -Dm755`. In a dev-linked checkout without another `omarchy-confirm` on `PATH`, an update cannot be confirmed. When an executable copy exists later on `PATH`, for example from the package, bash runs that copy instead. The new test fails either way.

**Suggested change:** `git update-index --chmod=+x bin/omarchy-confirm`.

### The new fzf check fails the bin style test

The fallback uses `if ! command -v fzf`. `test/shell.d/bin-style-test.sh` (lines 7-10) fails "bin commands use command helpers" for any file in `bin/` containing `command -v`, except `omarchy-cmd-*`, `omarchy-pkg-*` and `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`. A sandboxed run of that test exited 1 and listed `bin/omarchy-confirm`. The check scans every file in `bin/`, so restoring the executable bit does not change this.

**Impact:** `test/shell` fails on this branch independently of the mode problem.

**Suggested change:** use the repository's helper, `if ! omarchy-cmd-present fzf; then`, and adjust the test to match. Its fallback case sets `PATH` to a directory holding only `gum` and `awk`, so `omarchy-cmd-present` would be missing there too and the gum path would be taken for the wrong reason (with an fzf stub added to that directory, the changed helper still ran gum). Linking `$ROOT/bin/omarchy-cmd-present` into that directory, and putting `$ROOT/bin` on the `PATH` of `run_confirm` and the Python block, keeps the test from depending on an installed copy.

### Keys typed before the prompt appears can pick the wrong answer

fzf reads keys already pending at startup and can handle them before both rows have loaded (per fzf's source). `pos(2)` then lands on the only row present (Yes), and `accept` with no row exits 1. Key written to the terminal before the helper started, 100 runs per key:

| Key | Head | Head with `--sync` | `gum confirm` (20 runs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `n` | Yes in 4 | all correct | all correct |
| `q` | Yes in 3 | all correct | all correct |
| `y` | No in 73, each with `fzf failed (exit 1)` | all correct | all correct |

**Impact:** only affects a key typed before the prompt appears, for example `n` pressed while the "Ready to update?" box is being drawn. In the runs above, where the key was already typed before the helper started, `n` or `q` started the update or reboot in 3 to 4 percent of cases. Keys pressed after the rows are drawn behave correctly, and `gum confirm` had no such race.

**Suggested change:** add `--sync` to `fzf_args`, so fzf starts only after the input and `load` actions have completed. With it, the key, mouse, default-row and fallback checks gave the same results as without it. An earlier 60-run sample with `--sync` had one miss (`y` answered No).

### Conflict with current `quattro`

GitHub reports a merge conflict between this branch and `quattro`. `bin/omarchy-update-restart` conflicts because #9467 (merged 2026-09-25) added an unattended guard to `confirm_reboot`:

```bash
confirm_reboot() {
  if [[ ${OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED:-0} == "1" ]]; then
    echo "$1 Run omarchy-system-reboot when ready."
  elif omarchy-confirm "$1"; then   # this PR's change, applied to the quattro version
    omarchy-system-reboot
    exit 0
  fi
}
```

**Impact:** taking this PR's version of the function as is would drop the unattended guard, so `omarchy update -y` would prompt whenever a reboot is due.

**Suggested change:** resolve as above. On a local merge with the executable bit restored, the PR test passed, `--reboot-only` rebooted (stubbed) on `y` and not on `n`, and the unattended path printed the message without prompting. `quattro` now also has a `skip` test helper, which fits `pass "real fzf keyboard check skipped"` better after a rebase.

**Optional:** gum also toggles with `h`, `l` and Shift-Tab. These are unbound here, so `l` then Enter answers Yes, while gum's source toggles to No on `l` (the highlight does not move). Binding them, for example `h:up,l:down,btab:up` (not tested), would match gum. The comment above the status check says Esc gives 130 like gum, but gum 2.x exits 1 on Esc (only Ctrl-C gives 130). Callers treat both the same.

**Optional test improvement:** the real-fzf block waits with `os.waitpid(pid, 0)` and no timeout. Run against the previous helper, or with the `y`/`n`/`q` binds removed, it hangs until killed (60 s in these runs) instead of reporting `not ok`. A deadline loop with `os.WNOHANG` that kills the child on expiry (not tested) should make it fail cleanly.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up at 313900ae against the earlier findings, plus the new commit and its interaction with current `quattro`. Source review of the diff and callers, gum 2.0.2 and fzf 0.74.4 source, and the omarchy-pkgs PKGBUILDs. Sandboxed pseudo-terminal runs used real fzf 0.74.3 and gum 2.0.0 with scripted keys, synthetic mouse reports and a synthetic home directory. Reboot and shell restart were stubbed, and behaviour tests used an executable copy of the helper, with the committed mode tested separately. `omarchy update` was not run, no live terminal was clicked through, and the typeahead rate on a real terminal was not measured.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
